findings.title: Developer's local virtualenv (hypertools-dev/) ships inside the wheel and sdist and installs into every user's site-packages
findings.description: The repo root contains an untracked local virtualenv directory 'hypertools-dev/' (pyvenv.cfg, bin/, lib/...). Because pyproject.toml uses [tool.setuptools.packages.find] include=["hypertools*"] and the pyproject path enables namespace-package discovery by default (no __init__.py needed, no identifier check applied here), setuptools discovers 'hypertools-dev' as a top-level package. The built wheel therefore contains hypertools-dev/bin/activate_this.py (2383 bytes, virtualenv-project code: '# Copyright (c) 2020-202x The virtualenv developers'), the sdist contains hypertools-1.0.0.dev0/hypertools-dev/bin/activate_this.py, and dist-info/top_level.txt advertises two top-level packages: 'hypertools' and 'hypertools-dev'. pip install of the wheel then creates site-packages/hypertools-dev/bin/activate_this.py plus its compiled __pycache__/activate_this.cpython-312.pyc on every user machine (verified in the fresh venv; both files are listed in RECORD, so pip uninstall does clean them). Beyond shipping unrelated third-party code, this makes release artifact contents depend on whatever junk matches 'hypertools*' in the maintainer's working tree at build time. Fix: use the standard idiom include = ["hypertools", "hypertools.*"] (and/or set namespaces = false), and add hypertools-dev/ to .gitignore (see finding 005).
findings.repro: cd /Users/jmanning/hypertools && /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -m build --outdir /tmp/x5dist . && unzip -l /tmp/x5dist/hypertools-1.0.0.dev0-py3-none-any.whl | grep hypertools-dev && unzip -p /tmp/x5dist/hypertools-1.0.0.dev0-py3-none-any.whl hypertools-1.0.0.dev0.dist-info/top_level.txt
findings.expected: Wheel and sdist contain only the 'hypertools' package; top_level.txt lists only 'hypertools'; nothing outside the package installs into site-packages.
findings.actual: unzip -l: '2383  07-02-2026 12:30   hypertools-dev/bin/activate_this.py'; top_level.txt: 'hypertools\nhypertools-dev'; after pip install, site-packages RECORD contains 'hypertools-dev/bin/activate_this.py,sha256=wbmDks7G77k1IU4bsfJLDfUziWm0QB08gpfuVxxtRbQ,2383' and 'hypertools-dev/bin/__pycache__/activate_this.cpython-312.pyc,,'; os.listdir(site-packages) -> ['hypertools', 'hypertools-1.0.0.dev0.dist-info', 'hypertools-dev']

findings.title: hypertools/core/config.ini is missing from wheel and sdist, so hypertools.core.get_default_options()/apply_defaults() silently return empty defaults on every pip install
findings.description: hypertools/core/config.ini is the package's only non-.py data file ([plot] style/linestyle/linewidth/markersize/bigmarkersize/opacity/cmap=mako, [reduce] ndims=3 algorithm=IncrementalPCA, [align] algorithm=hyper, [cluster] n_clusters=3 verbose=False). There is no MANIFEST.in and no [tool.setuptools.package-data]/include-package-data configuration, so the file is absent from both the wheel and the sdist (verified: no .ini entry in either artifact; also absent from the previous build's SOURCES.txt). configurator.get_default_options() reads it via os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), 'config.ini'); with the file missing, datawrangler's configparser path silently yields nothing, so every hypertools section comes back {} on a pip-installed copy while a git checkout returns populated sections -- a silent dev-vs-installed API divergence with no warning. Empirically the blast radius today is limited to that exported API: grep shows zero internal callers of get_default_options/apply_defaults (hypertools/plot/backend.py:918 'bound_args.apply_defaults()' is inspect.BoundArguments, unrelated), and a controlled experiment in the same fresh venv (plot with vs without the file restored, cwd=/tmp, module path asserted) produced pixel-identical PNGs (max diff 0). Fix: add [tool.setuptools.package-data] 'hypertools.core' = ['config.ini'] (or a MANIFEST.in include + include-package-data), or remove the vestigial config machinery entirely (finding 003).
findings.repro:
unzip -l /tmp/x5dist/hypertools-1.0.0.dev0-py3-none-any.whl | grep -i '\.ini' ; # then in a fresh venv with the wheel installed, cwd outside the repo:
python -c "from hypertools.core import get_default_options; print(dict(get_default_options()['plot']))"
findings.expected: config.ini ships with the package; get_default_options()['plot'] returns {'style': '.', 'linestyle': '-', 'linewidth': '1', 'markersize': '4', 'bigmarkersize': '6', 'opacity': '0.7', 'cmap': 'mako'} as it does from the repo tree.
findings.actual: wheel/sdist contain no .ini file; fresh venv: "plot section: {}" and "AssertionError: plot defaults lost: {}" in the smoke test; os.path.exists(<site-packages>/hypertools/core/config.ini) -> False. Repo venv same call returns the populated dict. Pixel-diff of plots with/without the file: 'max pixel diff: 0 | pct differing: 0.0' (no visual impact today).

findings.title: config.ini / configurator machinery is vestigial: no code path consumes it, and its values duplicate hardcoded signature defaults
findings.description: configurator.py's docstring calls config.ini the 'Central default options for hypertools ... single source of truth', and hypertools/core/__init__.py exports get_default_options/apply_defaults -- but no module in the package calls either function (verified by grep; the only 'apply_defaults' hit is inspect's BoundArguments.apply_defaults in plot/backend.py:918). The behaviors config.ini claims to control actually come from hardcoded defaults (e.g. reduce() signature is 'reduce=\'IncrementalPCA\', ndims=None'; cluster's n_clusters=3 outcome reproduces with the config absent), which is why finding 002 has no visual impact. Either wire the config into the dispatchers or delete config.ini+configurator to stop advertising a configuration mechanism that does nothing. Related dead-code nit: hypertools/config.py retains a 'Fallback for Python < 3.8' importlib_metadata branch despite requires-python >=3.10.
findings.expected: A module described as central defaults should have at least one internal consumer (or not exist).
findings.actual: Only hit: 'hypertools/plot/backend.py:918:    bound_args.apply_defaults()' (inspect API, unrelated). Fresh venv without config.ini: cluster n_clusters=3 and reduce passthrough behavior identical to repo venv; plots pixel-identical.

findings.title: Build emits SetuptoolsDeprecationWarning: `project.license` as a TOML table is deprecated (future setuptools will fail the build)
findings.description: pyproject.toml declares license = { text = "MIT" }. setuptools 83 (resolved fresh in the isolated build env, so this is what any contributor gets) warns 4x during python -m build: 'SetuptoolsDeprecationWarning: `project.license` as a TOML table is deprecated -- Please use a simple string containing a SPDX expression'. When setuptools removes the deprecated path, release builds will start failing. Fix: license = "MIT" plus license-files = ["LICENSE"] per PEP 639; note SPDX license strings require setuptools>=77.0.3, so raise [build-system] requires from 'setuptools>=64' accordingly.
findings.expected: Clean build with no deprecation warnings from project metadata.
findings.actual: SetuptoolsDeprecationWarning: `project.license` as a TOML table is deprecated (emitted in both the sdist and wheel build environments)

findings.title: Repo hygiene enabling 001: hypertools-dev/ is untracked but NOT gitignored; stale dist/ (0.8.2 artifacts) and stale hypertools.egg-info sit in the repo root
findings.description: git check-ignore hypertools-dev -> not ignored; git ls-files hypertools-dev -> not tracked. Because it is not ignored, nothing flags it as junk and it silently feeds finding 001 on every build from this tree. Pre-existing build droppings (reported, not created by this audit's build, which left the tree untouched -- egg-info md5s unchanged, no build/ dir): (a) dist/ contains hypertools-0.8.2-py3-none-any.whl and hypertools-0.8.2.tar.gz dated Jan 29 -- stale artifacts two major versions old that could be uploaded by accident with a glob like 'twine upload dist/*'; (b) hypertools.egg-info/ (regenerated Jul 11 06:59 by an earlier build) whose top_level.txt already records the 'hypertools-dev' contamination. Fix: add hypertools-dev/ (or a general venv pattern) to .gitignore and clear stale dist/ artifacts before any release upload.

findings.title: Invalid normalize= value fails with a bare AssertionError that names a non-existent parameter ('scale_type')
findings.description: Hit during a realistic fresh-install workflow: hyp.analyze(data, normalize='zscore', reduce='PCA', ndims=3) -- plausible misuse since 'ZScore' is a hypertools manip model name -- raises from hypertools/tools/normalize.py:240 'AssertionError: scale_type must be across, within, row, none, or a fitted Normalizer.' Two problems: (1) the user-facing parameter is called 'normalize' (both in analyze() and normalize()), not 'scale_type', so the message points at a parameter the user never typed; (2) it is a bare assert, which produces AssertionError instead of ValueError/TypeError and is stripped under python -O, silently disabling the validation. The list of allowed values itself is helpful. Cross-unit note: normalize/analyze behavior units may also have caught this; filed here because it surfaced in the packaging fresh-install workflow.
findings.repro: python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; hyp.analyze(np.random.randn(120,15), normalize='zscore', reduce='PCA', ndims=3)"
findings.expected: ValueError naming the 'normalize' parameter, e.g.: ValueError: normalize must be one of 'across', 'within', 'row', None/False, or a fitted Normalizer (got 'zscore').
findings.actual:
File "...site-packages/hypertools/tools/normalize.py", line 240, in normalize
    assert (normalize in ['across', 'within', 'row', False, None]
AssertionError: scale_type must be across, within, row, none, or a fitted Normalizer.
